name: Kashi Chat Bhandar
why_it_matters: The Godowlia chaat counter that put Banarasi tamatar chaat — boiled potato mashed with stewed tomato, ghee and an aerial dusting of papdi — on the city's food map. Over 60 years in the same crossroads, served in clay bowls.
insider_tip: Order tamatar chaat first; the choora matar (poha-style flat rice with green peas) sells out by mid-evening. Standing room only — eat fast and step out.
signature_address: D 32/26, Godowlia Crossing, near Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Varanasi 221001

name: Deena Chaat Bhandar
why_it_matters: Started by Deena Nath Kesari on a head-carried khomcha in the late 1960s, now a 50+ year Luxa Road institution. The tamatar chaat gravy is slow-cooked for hours with mustard oil, jaggery, and dried fruit — denser and tangier than the Godowlia version.
insider_tip: Opens at 2pm, not lunchtime — built around evening temple foot traffic. The palak patta chaat (crisp-fried spinach leaves topped with dahi and chutney) is the second order locals make.
signature_address: Hanuman Mandir, Ramapura Luxa Road, Luxa, Varanasi 221001

name: The Ram Bhandar
why_it_matters: A breakfast counter in the narrow lanes of Thatheri Bazaar near Kashi Vishwanath, in operation for over 150 years. Cooks in pure desi ghee — the badi kachori and saffron jalebi are what locals queue for from 7am.
insider_tip: Open 7-11am only. Last stretch is two-wheeler-or-foot from Chowk; arrive before 8am or you'll wait. No-onion, no-garlic aloo-chana sabzi — flag heat-sensitive eaters.
signature_address: Thatheri Bazaar, near Kashi Vishwanath, Chowk, Varanasi 221001

name: Madhur Milan Cafe
why_it_matters: Open-fronted breakfast cafe near the Vishwanath Gali entrance — chefs flip dosas and kachoris in full street view. The default morning stop for ghat-goers heading back from sunrise aarti.
insider_tip: Limited indoor seats; standing-and-eating is the norm. Open 8am-9pm; the kachori sabzi runs out by mid-morning, dosas and pav bhaji carry the rest of the day.
signature_address: Dashashwamedh Road, near Vishwanath Gali Gate, Varanasi 221001

name: Blue Lassi Shop
why_it_matters: An eight-foot lane shop in Kachori Gali near Manikarnika Ghat, founded in 1925 and now in its third generation. 50+ lassi varieties served thick in kulhads, topped with chopped fruit, malai and crushed nuts — the city's reference point for Banarasi lassi.
insider_tip: Sit on the wooden bench outside and watch the funeral processions pass towards Manikarnika — the proximity is unsettling but the shop has run alongside it for a century. Cash only.
signature_address: CK 1/40, Kachori Gali, Bangali Tola, Varanasi 221001

name: Pahalwan Lassi
why_it_matters: An 8x12-foot stall at Malviya Chauraha on Lanka Road, named for Panna Sardar — a pre-Independence wrestler whose customers christened the shop 'pehelwan'. His sons now run multiple branches around BHU; the original is still the densest pour.
insider_tip: At least 3-4 lookalike 'pehelwan' shops sit beside each other on Lanka Road — extended family, all from the same stock. Locals point to the Malviya Chauraha original; ask for the 'asli' if you're unsure.
signature_address: Malviya Chauraha, Lanka Road, near BHU Gate, Varanasi 221005
